name: treecc
why: An aspect-oriented tree compiler generator from the DotGNU project, a rare look at how compilers get built from declarative specs.

brief.what_it_is: Treecc is a compiler-compiler from the DotGNU project that generates C (or C++) code for building and walking compiler parse trees. You write a declarative spec in treecc's own rule-based syntax, listing node types with their fields and abstract superclasses, plus 'operation' definitions that give per-node-type code for things like type inference. Embedded C code supplies the details. Treecc emits the node structures, the '*_create' constructor functions, and the operation dispatch code, and it reports an error when an operation lacks a case for some node type.
brief.why_it_exists: The manual argues that lex and yacc stop at parsing and leave semantic analysis and code generation to hand-written tree code, which is error-prone. Adding a node type means finding every walker that must handle it, and the Visitor pattern makes adding node types painful. Treecc aims to catch coverage gaps automatically.
brief.how_it_works: The yacc grammar's semantic actions call the generated '*_create' functions to build the tree, and the parameters match the node's fields in type and order. Each operation is declared once, with a case per node type, and abstract types such as 'binary' let one case cover all subclasses. A more specific case, such as one for 'power', overrides the inherited one. Treecc checks that every concrete node type is covered and raises an error if one is missing, so a newly added node type that an operation does not handle is caught at translation time.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the brew install was visible in the pages I read. Section 3 of the manual, 'Invoking treecc from the command-line', was listed in the table of contents but I did not fetch it, so I have no command syntax from the manual.
brief.standout: Treecc applies aspect-oriented ideas to compiler trees. Each operation is a cross-cutting aspect that gets woven across all node types, and the generator checks coverage globally, which the manual says ordinary OO and Visitor designs do not do. It also keeps the spec declarative and yacc-like rather than inventing a new language.
brief.status: Unknown. The only dated item is the manual, generated by Klaus Treichel on January 18, 2009 with texi2html 1.78. I found no release, commit, or changelog information in the pages I read, so the project looks quiet from the documentation alone.
brief.caveats: The homepage is only a manual index. The content is in sub-pages, and the entry is based on sections 1 and 2 only. The example uses yacc-style grammars, so treecc is tied to a yacc workflow. The manual says the generated code is C, C++, or another underlying language, so target-language support beyond C is not explained. The manual is from 2009 and I could not confirm whether it matches current releases. The brew description was 'Aspect-oriented approach to writing compilers'.
quotes: The approach that we take with "treecc" is similar to that used by "yacc".
The translator is responsible for generating the tree building and walking code, and for checking that all relevant operations have been implemented on the node types.
If it detects a lack, it will immediately raise an error to the user.
